Synopsis:
    Haldia Petrochemicals (HPL) is pursuing a cracker retrofit with Lummus to achieve up to 30% LPG substitution flexibility, driven by severe naphtha supply disruptions caused by near-halted Strait of Hormuz shipments amid the U.S.-Iran war. The company has existing term contracts with QatarEnergy, Kuwait Petroleum, and ADNOC but was forced into the spot market. It is sourcing LPG domestically from IPPL and exploring global import options. HPL operates a major petrochemicals complex in West Bengal with 700k tons/year ethylene capacity, and plans an acetone/phenol plant opening in October.
